Silencing The Mind S Chatter

# Silencing The Mind S Chatter

## Verbatim Discourse Excerpts
How can I have a quiet mind? A beautiful question. Is your mind very noisy now? Yes. What is the noise around? He was thinking about how can he properly ask the question. Okay. So your mind was thinking about the future. Then what else does your mind think? And he was thinking, what time is lunch? What time? What time is lunch is a very simple thought. It's not going to hurt.

How many of you are hungry? So that is the nature of the mind. The nature of the mind is to take you into a future. Your future has been about the question and the food. Or it would take you into a past which would be your hurts, your disappointment, your sadness, your uncomfortable experience. That is what mind is capable of. So in order to quieten that mind, what you need to do to start with is do the serene mind practice.

## Key Teachings
- Your mind will say, what if she's going to speak longer and my food is going to get delayed? — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- So your mind was thinking about the future. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- The nature of the mind is to take you into a future. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji

## Source Context
- Video: How to silence the continuous chatter of the mind?

- Speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji

Cruelty And The Need For Empathy

# Cruelty And The Need For Empathy

## Verbatim Discourse Excerpts
Let us return to our soul. Let us reconnect with who we actually are. Let us take a few moments and seek forgiveness from all mother earth's creatures. Please close your eyes. Place your palms on your heart and internally apologize to every living being on whom you may have perpetrated cruelty. Let us all ask forgiveness from that mother elephant who suffered agony, lost her own life and that of a baby helplessly.

Today is world environment day. It is sad. We have to talk of the heartless killing of a pregnant elephant. Have you ever looked into the eyes of an elephant? They are far more sensitive, kind and family oriented than most human beings. A mother elephant holds a baby for 18 to 22 months in a womb which is two times longer than a human mother does. How could we do something so heartless to a creature as magnificent as her?

## Key Teachings
- Place your palms on your heart and internally apologize to every living being on whom you may have perpetrated cruelty. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- We have to talk of the heartless killing of a pregnant elephant. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- Have you ever looked into the eyes of an elephant? — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji

The Call To Inner Peace

# The Call To Inner Peace

## Verbatim Discourse Excerpts
How can we hurt each other without these thoughts in our infected minds? Internally, you are never at peace for long. You are never restful. There is always a disturbance. You are internally angry with your partner, with your mother, with your father, child, colleague, boss and neighbor. Should not your inner complaining stop? Is it not time for you to become peaceful with everyone and with yourself?

This, sadly, is the state of an unawakened human being. Do you really want to live this way with anger and a strong desire to dominate and control? It is time you rose towards Mukthi or enlightenment. It is time you awaken to your true nature of immense peacefulness. It is important that millions wake up from their unawakened state of inner conflict and move towards an awakened state of peace.

## Key Teachings
- It is important that millions wake up from their unawakened state of inner conflict and move towards an awakened state of peace. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- To awaken to peace and to spread that peace around us is the ultimate dharma of every human being on this planet. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
- Internally, you are never at peace for long. — Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji

These intense negative emotions highlight the profound consequences of unforgiveness, demonstrating how holding onto such states can lead to significant personal distress and a loss of inner peace.

The destructive impulse to put others down in order to feel superior is a profound symptom of "I-Consciousness"—a fragmented state of separation that breeds comparison, judgment, and conflict. This divisive mindset arises from a lack of inner healing and a misguided sense of isolation, which prevents individuals from realizing their true, interconnected nature. True spiritual awakening lies in transcending this "I-Consciousness" to awaken to "Oneness," where the artificial hierarchies of superiority and inferiority dissolve. By recognizing that our authentic self-worth is not built on external comparisons or the belittlement of others, we can heal our inner divisions. Ultimately, moving beyond this judgmental framework allows us to restore harmony within ourselves and with Mother Earth, resolving the root of humanity's conflicts through a shared, unified existence.
